faq.q: What is the price difference between Azimut 39 and Mangusta 80?
faq.a: The Azimut 39 costs €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, all inclusive. The Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours, which includes a free jet ski. So for a half-day trip, the Mangusta 80 is about €2,420 more expensive, but includes a jet ski.

faq.q: Which boat is better for a large group?
faq.a: Both can accommodate 12 passengers, but the Azimut 39 takes 11 pax and the Mangusta 80 takes 12 pax. For groups of 10-11, the Azimut 39 is more cost-effective. For exactly 12, the Mangusta 80 is the only option that fits everyone comfortably.

faq.q: Does the Mangusta 80 include a jet ski?
faq.a: Yes, the Mangusta 80 charter (minimum 4 hours) includes a free jet ski. The Azimut 39 does not include a jet ski, but you can add one for an extra fee – ask via WhatsApp for a custom quote.

faq.q: What is included in the Azimut 39 charter price?
faq.a: The Azimut 39 price includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). No hidden costs.

faq.q: Can I book the Mangusta 80 for less than 4 hours?
faq.a: No, the Mangusta 80 has a minimum charter duration of 4 hours. The Azimut 39 can be booked for as little as 2 hours, making it more flexible for short trips.

Both are powerful motor yachts. The Azimut 39 (12.5m) is a sporty cruiser with good speed, while the Mangusta 80 (24m) is a larger, comfortable yacht. Exact speeds depend on conditions, but the Azimut 39 is generally quicker for its size.

faq.q: Where do both boats depart from?
faq.a: Both the Azimut 39 and Mangusta 80 depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella. You can easily reach the marina from anywhere on the Costa del Sol.

faq.q: How do I book either boat?
faq.a: You can book directly through our website or contact us via WhatsApp for availability and custom requests. Prices are as listed, and we recommend booking in advance, especially during peak season.

data.body_html:
Choosing between the Azimut 39 and the Mangusta 80 for your Marbella boat charter in 2035? This cost comparison breaks down the key differences in price, capacity, and inclusions to help you decide. Both yachts depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT – but the costs vary significantly.

Azimut 39 Pricing (Tier A)

The Azimut 39 is a 12.5m sporty cruiser accommodating up to 11 passengers. It falls under our Tier A pricing:

  • €749 for 2 hours
  • €2,299 for 8 hours (full day)

All prices include skipper, fuel, drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava), light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees.

Mangusta 80 Pricing (Tier B)

The Mangusta 80 is a 24m luxury yacht with a capacity of 12 passengers. It is priced under Tier B:

  • €4,719 minimum 4 hours (includes free jet ski)

This price includes the same inclusions as the Azimut 39, plus a jet ski. Longer durations are available on request via WhatsApp.

Cost Per Person Comparison

For a full-day charter (8 hours), the Azimut 39 costs €2,299, which works out to approximately €209 per person (based on 11 passengers). The Mangusta 80 for 4 hours costs €4,719, or about €393 per person (based on 12 passengers). While the Mangusta 80 is more expensive per person, it includes a jet ski and offers more space and luxury.

Which Boat Should You Choose?

If you have a smaller group (up to 11) and want a budget-friendly option, the Azimut 39 is ideal. For larger groups (up to 12) or if you want a jet ski included, the Mangusta 80 offers better value despite the higher upfront cost. Both boats depart from Puerto Banús and provide a premium Marbella experience.

Booking and Customisation

All bookings can be made via WhatsApp for custom durations or special requests. Prices are fixed for the standard packages listed above. For more information on our entire fleet, visit our boat rental Marbella hub.

Frequently asked questions

What is the price difference between Azimut 39 and Mangusta 80?

The Azimut 39 costs €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, all inclusive. The Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours, which includes a free jet ski. So for a half-day trip, the Mangusta 80 is about €2,420 more expensive, but includes a jet ski.

Which boat is better for a large group?

Both can accommodate 12 passengers, but the Azimut 39 takes 11 pax and the Mangusta 80 takes 12 pax. For groups of 10-11, the Azimut 39 is more cost-effective. For exactly 12, the Mangusta 80 is the only option that fits everyone comfortably.

Does the Mangusta 80 include a jet ski?

Yes, the Mangusta 80 charter (minimum 4 hours) includes a free jet ski. The Azimut 39 does not include a jet ski, but you can add one for an extra fee – ask via WhatsApp for a custom quote.

What is included in the Azimut 39 charter price?

The Azimut 39 price includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). No hidden costs.

Can I book the Mangusta 80 for less than 4 hours?

No, the Mangusta 80 has a minimum charter duration of 4 hours. The Azimut 39 can be booked for as little as 2 hours, making it more flexible for short trips.

Which boat is faster?

Both are powerful motor yachts. The Azimut 39 (12.5m) is a sporty cruiser with good speed, while the Mangusta 80 (24m) is a larger, comfortable yacht. Exact speeds depend on conditions, but the Azimut 39 is generally quicker for its size.

Where do both boats depart from?

Both the Azimut 39 and Mangusta 80 depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella. You can easily reach the marina from anywhere on the Costa del Sol.

How do I book either boat?

You can book directly through our website or contact us via WhatsApp for availability and custom requests. Prices are as listed, and we recommend booking in advance, especially during peak season.
